si_3_author_journal_and_year: Erin L. Martin et al., Drug and Alcohol Dependence Reports, 2025
si_4_title: Sex differences in normative modeling of cortical thickness in cannabis use disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: SINGLE-SITE refers to the clinical cohorts of individuals with cannabis use disorder (CUD) recruited from two clinical trials at the Medical University of South Carolina (NCT02892110 and NCT03144232). None (Pre-Trained NM) refers to the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which utilizes a pre-existing normative reference population.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The present study used pre-treatment baseline data from two clinical trials for CUD at the Medical University of South Carolina. ... The aseg.stats file for each participant was then input into the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which computes normative z-scores of participant-level measurements relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18 -100 (n = 6909)...
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Martin2025.pdf.md: 2.1 Participants; 2.3 MRI acquisition and normative modeling

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The SINGLE-SITE clinical trial cohorts (n=72) are used as the patient group for clinical research to evaluate sex differences in brain morphometry. NOMIS provides the pre-trained normative reference population (n=6909) used to compute individual z-scores for the CUD patients.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: we tested for differences in normed z-scores between males and females with CUD using baseline data from two clinical trials. ... NOMIS ... computes normative z-scores ... relative to a large sample of healthy adults ... (n = 6909)
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Martin2025.pdf.md: 1. Introduction; 2.3 MRI acquisition and normative modeling

dc_3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.detail: The study utilizes the NOMIS software, which uses a reference sample of 6,909 healthy adults to compute z-scores. The training N for the specific regression models used by NOMIS is not reported in the current study as it uses the pre-trained version.
dc_3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.supporting_text: NOMIS ... computes normative z-scores ... relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18 -100 (n = 6909)

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: The NOMIS reference sample age range is 18-100 years as stated in the text. Mean age (55.0) and SD (20.0) are retrieved from the explicitly cited external source (Potvin et al., 2022) which describes the development of the NOMIS normative sample.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: Sex distribution for the NOMIS sample (56.8% female) is obtained from the cited external source (Potvin et al., 2022). female_n is calculated as 6909 * 0.568 = 3924.3 (rounded to 3924). male_n is inferred by subtracting female_n from the total N (6909 - 3924 = 2985).
